newsitem.title: THAILAND: Student exiles demand Burma honours 1990 polls.
newsitem.headline: Student exiles demand Burma honours 1990 polls.

text.p: A group of exiled Burmese students protested in front of Rangoon's embassy in Bangkok on Tuesday to demand that an opposition party's landslide victory in 1990 elections be recognised by the Rangoon military junta.
The students, joined by some Thai counterparts, carried placards and posters at a peaceful protest outside the embassy to mark the seventh anniversary of the polls.
Opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party easily won the election but the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) refused to honour the result.

"In commemoration of the seventh anniversary of the NLD'S election victory, we, the democracy-loving Thai and Burmese students, strongly comdemn the SLORC rulers for their suppression of political freedom and violations of human rights in Burma," a joint statement by the students said.

"We urge the SLORC to honour the promise made to the Burmese people by allowing the NLD, the party that has won the election, to form the government and then transfer power to a democratically-elected government," it added.
Hundreds of Burmese dissidents fled to Thailand after the military crushed pro-democracy street protests in Rangoon in September 1988.
Some were repatriated by Thai authorities to Burma in early 1990 but many others still remain in Thailand.
In Rangoon on Tuesday, a small group of NLD members held a gathering at Suu Kyi's home to mark the election anniversary. The SLORC refused to permit a larger gathering.
